reasons.j1: Clarke's cut stops at 'non respondeat ad exemplar', about half the page, so the second half is judged on the Latin alone. The six are near-identical and complete to 'ambitu circuit,'; all follow the 1515 print's 'afflent' ('blow upon') and 'Vides enim', which is the source as given. They separate only on 'aries † excolitur': [T02a] keeps 'is perfected' and notes it means rises (= margin 'exoritur', Clarke 'rises in a moment'); [T0a]–[T1a] write 'is passed through', [T0a]/[T1c]/[T1a] with conjectures that ignore the margin; [T0a] also has 'gulls' for 'Fulicæ'.
reasons.j2: Reference stops at 'non respondeat ad exemplar' while the page runs on to 'ambitu circuit'. All six cover the whole page and render the OCR's 'afflent' literally ('blow upon'; reference: deceive the eye), which I do not penalise. [T1a]-[T1c] give 'passed through' for 'excolitur' (margin 'exoritur'); [T02a] keeps the word and notes it means rising. [T0a] also has 'gulls' for 'Fulicae'.
